chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about exchanging dirhams for dirhams, and about the surplus/excess between them, so he said: 'If there is copper or gold between them, there is no objection.'

key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging dirhams for dirhams if they differ in purity or contain gold/copper?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the rules of *bay' al-thahib bi al-thahib* (exchange of silver for silver), ruling that if the dirhams contain copper or gold, the exchange is permissible even with inequality. This indicates that the strict condition of equal weight (*ta'adud*) applies primarily to pure silver dirhams, while mixed or different compositions allow for flexibility in value or weight, reflecting the practical economic realities of the time. The hadith underscores the Shia juristic principle that *riba* (usury) in commodity exchange is contingent upon the homogeneity and purity of the goods being exchanged.
